s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation, occurring in the context of immunotherapy
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous eosinophils on biopsy and pruritic rash

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular inflammation on biopsy and rash characteristics

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Rash onset after immunotherapy initiation and lack of response to terbinafine

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Rash onset after immunotherapy initiation and lack of response to terbinafine

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous annular plaques without scale and rash progression

raw.rationale: The patient's rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship between the immunotherapy and the rash, and the biopsy findings are consistent with an immune-mediated reaction.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows numerous eosinophils, the clinical presentation and temporal relationship to immunotherapy initiation more strongly support a drug-induced rash.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not specifically indicate vasculitis, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with a drug-induced rash.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: While ipilimumab could also be the culprit, pembrolizumab is a more likely cause given its known association with skin reactions, and the temporal relationship to the start of the immunotherapy regimen.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically support this diagnosis, and the temporal relationship to immunotherapy initiation suggests a drug-induced rash.
